Request for Proposal (RFP)
Migration from On-Premises Microsoft CRM to Microsoft Dynamics
365 Cloud
Request for Proposals released: 3/30/2026
Responses due: 4/29/2026 at 5:00pm PDT

1.

Introduction and Background
Energy Trust of Oregon, Inc. (Energy Trust), an Oregon nonprofit corporation, is soliciting
proposals from qualified vendors to plan, design, and execute the migration of our existing
on‑premises Microsoft CRM implementation to the Microsoft Dynamics 365 cloud CRM
platform.

It is Energy Trust’s intention to solicit qualifications from a wide range of multiple
respondents.

Energy Trust will examine all responses carefully and select a single
respondent to provide these services.

Energy Trust is an independent nonprofit organization selected and overseen by the Oregon
Public Utility Commission (OPUC) to help Oregon utility customers save energy and generate
renewable power.

Energy Trust’s services, cash incentives and energy solutions have helped
participating customers of Portland General Electric, Pacific Power, NW Natural, Cascade
Natural Gas and Avista save nearly $8.9 billion on their energy bills.

The cumulative impact
of the organization’s leadership since 2002 has been a contributing factor in the region’s
low energy costs and in building a sustainable energy future.

To learn more about Energy
Trust please visit www.energytrust.org/about.

Our organization currently operates Microsoft Dynamics Customer Engagement 9.1 on
premises (referred to as Microsoft CRM on‑premises in this RFP), supporting a single
business unit and mission‑critical customer relationship management processes.

We seek an
experienced Microsoft partner to deliver a secure, scalable, and well‑governed migration
that modernizes our CRM capabilities while minimizing business disruption.

Description of Current CRM On-premises Implementation


See Appendix A

3.

RFP Objectives
The objectives of this RFP are to:
1






Select a vendor with deep expertise in Microsoft Dynamics 365 cloud migrations
Ensure a secure, compliant,

and low‑risk transition from on‑premises CRM to the
cloud
Maintain current CRM capabilities while preserving required functionality and
integrations
Establish a foundation for future innovation using the suite of Microsoft CRM 365
functionality as well as related Microsoft technologies

4.

Scope of Services
The selected vendor will be expected to provide end‑to‑end services covering planning,
migration, validation, and post‑go‑live support.

At a minimum, the scope of services shall
include the following components.

4.1 Discovery and Assessment
The vendor shall conduct a comprehensive assessment of the existing on‑premises CRM
environment, including but not limited to:









Current Microsoft CRM version, architecture, licensing, and deployment model
Custom entities, fields, forms, workflows, plugins,

and JavaScript
Integrations with third‑party systems, internal applications, and data sources
Security model, roles, teams, and access controls
Data volumes, data quality, and retention requirements
Reporting, dashboards,

and analytics usage
Dependencies on legacy technologies or unsupported components
Cost modeling based on current data volumes, usage, and user counts

Deliverables shall include an assessment report identifying risks, constraints, dependencies,
cost considerations, and recommended remediation,

cost efficiency and modernization
actions.

4.2 Migration Strategy and Solution Design
The vendor shall define a detailed migration strategy and target‑state solution design,
including:




Recommended Dynamics 365 applications and licensing (e.g., Sales, Customer
Service, Marketing)
Tenant, environment (multiple environments for development, testing,

staging and
production), and region strategy aligned with organizational governance
Data migration approach (phased vs. full, historical vs. active data)
2









Approach for current replication of database to a read-only database for reporting,
analysis, and as a data source for an internal transaction system.

Nightly updates to on premises data warehouse
Customization and extension strategy leveraging out‑of‑the‑box capabilities, Power
Platform, and Azure services
Integration architecture using supported APIs, connectors, and middleware
Identity and access management design (e.g., Entra ID/Azure AD integration)
Security,

compliance, and data residency considerations
Decommissioning strategy for the on‑premises CRM environment

The vendor shall produce a formal solution design document for review and approval.

4.3 Configuration, Customization, and Modernization
The vendor shall partner with internal product owner to configure and extend Dynamics 365
to meet business requirements, including:







Re‑implementation or refactoring of existing customizations
Migration from unsupported plugins or code to supported cloud patterns
Implementation of Power Automate flows, Power Apps, and business rules as
appropriate
Configuration of security roles, teams, and field‑level security
Setup of dashboards,

views, and reporting

Where feasible, the vendor is expected to contrast simplification and modernization to
direct “lift‑and‑shift” replication of legacy functionality for the internal product team’s
consideration and decision.

4.4 Data Migration
The vendor shall plan and support internal team in executing secure and accurate data
migration activities, including:







Data mapping and transformation
Data cleansing and validation
Migration of core and related entities
Handling of attachments, notes,

and activities
Reconciliation and data quality verification
Support for multiple test migrations prior to production cutover

The vendor shall create a plan to ensure data integrity, auditability, and minimal downtime
during final cutover.

4.5 Integration, Migration and Validation
The vendor shall partner with internal software engineering team to migrate, redesign, or
replace integrations with external systems, including:




ERP, finance, marketing automation, and customer support systems
Custom applications and data warehouses
Email,

document management, and collaboration tools

All integrations must comply with Microsoft‑supported cloud integration patterns and
security best practices.

4.6 Testing and Quality Assurance
The vendor shall partner with internal product owners to develop and execute a
comprehensive testing strategy, including:







Unit and system testing
Integration testing
User acceptance testing (UAT) support
Performance and scalability testing (as applicable)
Security and role‑based access testing

Defects must be documented, prioritized, and resolved prior to production deployment.

Energy Trust product owner will approve acceptable resolution of defects in collaboration
with vendor.

4.7 Training and Change Management
The vendor shall support organizational adoption through co-development (with internal
product owner) of the following artifacts:






Administrator and power‑user training
End‑user training materials and sessions tailored to Energy Trust’s environment
Knowledge transfer to internal IT teams
Documentation covering configuration, integrations, and support procedures

4.8 Go‑Live and Post‑Implementation Support
The vendor shall provide:
4






Cutover planning and execution support
Go‑live readiness assessment
Active support period following go‑live
Transition to steady‑state support and operations

5.

Project Management and Governance
Energy Trust will provide a dedicated project manager and follow a structured project
management methodology.

If additional project management is proposed by the vendor,
the proposal should describe:




Project governance model
Communication and reporting approach
Risk and issue management approach

6.

Vendor Qualifications
Vendors should demonstrate:





Proven experience migrating on‑premises Microsoft CRM to Dynamics 365 cloud
Microsoft partner status and relevant certifications
Experience with organizations of similar size and complexity
References from comparable projects

7.

Proposal Submission Requirements
Responses must be submitted via email.

A maximum length of 15 pages (does not include
required Representations and Signature page or cover letter) will be accepted.

You must disclose any direct or indirect, actual or potential conflicts of interest with Energy
Trust.

Include a signed and completed Representations and Signature page, in the form attached
to this RFQ as Appendix B, certifying the representations stated therein (outside the 15-page
limit).

Proposals must include:



Cover letter describing your company’s background and proficiency
Executive summary
5







Detailed approach and methodology
Scope assumptions and exclusions
Project timeline and resource plan
Pricing and licensing assumptions
Risk identification and mitigation strategies

9.

Selection Criteria
Response selection will be the sole responsibility of Energy Trust and will be undertaken at
the sole discretion of Energy Trust.

Responses may be eliminated from consideration at
Energy Trust’s sole discretion for any reason, including but not limited to:

•
•
•
•

The response is substantially incomplete or exceeds page limits
The response does not address the objectives and requirements of this RFP
Response is inconsistent with Energy Trust policies or requirements
A conflict of interest exists that cannot be mitigated

Responses will be evaluated by the following

criteria:
•
•
•

Quality of Response - Clarity and completeness
Capabilities - Demonstrated capability to provide the services sought
Pricing – Competitiveness and clarity

Energy Trust also reserves the right to change the criteria used to evaluate responses.

Responding companies may inquire about the status of their response via email
(kevin.hoffmann@energytrust.org).

Specifically, they may inquire about the receipt and
6

condition of response materials and receive an update as to whether their responses are
still under consideration.

All responding companies will receive notification when a
contractor has been selected.

Terms and Conditions

Energy Trust reserves the right, in its sole discretion, to reject any or all responses in whole
or in part, to waive any minor irregularities or informalities in a response, and to enter into
any agreement deemed to be in its best interests.

In addition to any other enumerated
reserved rights and/or options as stated in this RFP, Energy Trust may in its sole discretion
do any one or more of the following:
•
•
•
•

•
•
•
•
•

Determine which responses are eligible for consideration in response to this RFP.
Disqualify responses that do not meet the requirements.
Negotiate with respondents to amend any response.

Select and negotiate and/or enter into agreements with respondents who are most
responsive to the RFP and whose responses best satisfy the interests of Energy Trust
and not necessarily on the basis of price alone or any other single factor.

Issue additional subsequent solicitations for responses, including withdrawing this
RFP at any time and/or issuing a new RFP that would supersede and replace this one.
Vary any timetable or schedule, add or change any provisions discussed herein.
Conduct any briefing session or further RFP process on any terms and conditions.
Suspend or modify the RFP process at any time.
Enter into relationships with more than one respondent.

10.1 Confidentiality
Respondents shall clearly identify only those portions of their proposals that they do not
want revealed to third parties and label such portions as “Confidential Information”.

Except
as required under law or for regulatory purposes Energy Trust will maintain confidentiality
of such information.

Energy Trust will not accept proposals or other documents that are
marked to indicate the entire document is the confidential or proprietary information of the
sender or that restricted handling is required.

Normal business practices will be observed in
handling proposal materials.

Except in the case of litigation or other legal disclosure and/or
audit requirements, Energy Trust will not disclose information submitted in response to an
RFP to any third party.

10.2 No Commitment/Resulting Contract
This RFP does not constitute an offer by Energy Trust, nor does it commit Energy Trust to
enter into a contract or similar undertaking with any of the respondents or any organization
associated with any of the respondents.

Energy Trust reserves the right to enter into
relationships with more than one respondent.

Energy Trust also reserves the right to
suspend or modify the RFP process or to issue a new RFP for the services described that
would supersede and replace this one.

No binding obligation shall be created unless Energy
Trust or its representative and the concerned parties execute a binding agreement.

Final selection implies that Energy Trust and the selected respondent expect to reach a
contractual agreement which would outline the roles and responsibilities of all parties.

No
award will be considered a commitment until a written contract has been executed by
Energy Trust with the selected respondent(s).
The contract term cannot exceed two years.

10.3 No Reassignment
All responses shall state that in the event of an award from Energy Trust, the resulting
contract(s) and obligations shall not be sold or reassigned without the written permission of
Energy Trust.

10.4 Conflict of Interest Disclosure
Respondents shall disclose in their response all direct or indirect, actual or potential
conflicts of interest it or any of their personnel may have with Energy Trust.

A "direct or
indirect conflict" is defined as any situation in which an individual has or may be reasonably
construed to have a direct or indirect personal or financial interest in any business affairs of
Energy Trust,

whether because of a proposed contract or transaction to which Energy Trust
may be a party or may be interested or is under consideration, or whether such conflict is
purely conceptual, because of similarity of business interests or affairs.

If such conflict of
interest does or may exist at the time respondents submit their proposal, respondents must
include a conflict of interest mitigation strategy in their proposal.

10.5 Validity and Deadlines
All responses shall specify the date through which the response is valid.

At a minimum,
responses shall be valid through 8/31/2026.

10.6 Waiver of Claims and Response Costs
The candidate waives any right it may have to bring any claim, whether in damages or
equity, against Energy Trust, its Board, agents, employees or contractors, with respect to
any matter arising out of any process associated with this RFP.

This RFP does not obligate
Energy Trust to pay any costs incurred by any respondent in the preparation or submission
of a response.
Once submitted, responses will not be returned to respondents.

10.7 RFP Clarification/Interpretation
Any clarification or interpretation of the RFP documents shall be issued in writing by Energy
Trust.

Oral instructions or information concerning the RFP given out by Energy Trust
employees or agents to prospective respondents shall not bind Energy Trust.

10.8 Additional Information
Energy Trust may request additional information prior to final selection.
